newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Franco-German pledge to drive Europe irks Dutch.
newsitem.headline: Franco-German pledge to drive Europe irks Dutch.

text.p: A Franco-German pledge to drive European integration ahead on Monday ruffled feathers in the Netherlands, holders of the six-month Euro-presidency.

"The actions of France and Germany...undermine the Dutch presidency and are characteristic of the crass way in which the large member states within the European Union ignore the smaller ones," Frans Weisglas, foreign affairs spokesman for the ruling Liberal VVD coalition party, told Reuters.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel and his French counterpart Herve de Charette told a joint news conference in Brussels on Monday their two countries were committed to being Europe's engine.
Dutch broadcast media described the Franco-German move as a slap in the face for the presidency and spoke of a "coup against the Dutch".
Weisglas said he would press Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok openly to reprimand France and Germany for their behaviour.
"We would like (the government) to make it clear that this action is not appreciated," he said.
"It is arrogant and it is not effective...of course if Germany and France want to support the Dutch presidency we welcome it but this is a strange way of doing it."
Christian Democrat MP Yvonne van Rooy said she would ask Kok whether the Franco-German move had been requested by the Dutch.
"(It) doesn't show a great deal of respect for the Netherlands," Dutch press agency ANP quoted her as saying.
